public_rationale: On September 27, 2024, CNBC reported that OpenAI expected about $5 billion in company-wide losses on $3.7 billion in revenue for 2024; this was a projection, not a realized full-cost LLM-service result [e1]. Alphabet's fourth-quarter 2024 disclosure reports broad segments and places general-model development among shared costs [e2]. Meta's 2024 disclosure reports Family of Apps and Reality Labs without separate LLM accounts [e3]. These sources establish neither losses and continuing dependence on financial support outside service earnings across all four named businesses nor a service that covered its full costs from its own earnings [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: CNBC had not seen OpenAI's accounts, and the reported loss estimate excluded stock compensation and some other expenses [e1].
The packet contains no usable Anthropic financial evidence.
Alphabet's and Meta's broader results cannot establish standalone LLM-service profitability or dependence on financial support [e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs run by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta are unprofitable and unsustainable.

statement.excerpt: As I've written about many, many, many times, the Large Language Models run by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta are unprofitable and unsustainable, and the transformer-based architecture they run on has peaked.

our_interpretation: The nearby explanation expressly cites 2024 losses, so calendar 2024 is the target period.
The claim concerns the economics of the named companies' LLM services, rather than consolidated corporate profitability.
The ordinary reading of unprofitable is that attributable revenue does not cover full development and operating costs.
The minimum testable reading of unsustainable is dependence on continuing financial support outside the services' own earnings. No bankruptcy deadline is supplied.
The nearby reported private-company figures imply an estimate basis; they do not establish GAAP or another consistent accounting standard for all four businesses.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable 2024 revenue and full-cost evidence establishes losses and dependence on outside financial support for the named LLM businesses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that a named LLM business covered its full costs and could sustain its operations from its own earnings during 2024.

evidence.explanation: This supports concern about OpenAI's economics, but reports expected company-wide losses rather than realized LLM-service results. CNBC says it had not seen the accounts, and reports that the estimate excludes stock compensation and other incompletely explained expenses.
The release places general-model development among shared costs and reports broader business segments. Those disclosures cannot establish a standalone profit or loss for Google's LLM services.
Meta's reported segments do not separate LLM revenue and costs. Its consolidated or segment profitability therefore cannot settle the claim about LLM services.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable realized calendar-2024 LLM-service revenue and full attributable costs for all four businesses, plus evidence of whether each required continuing financial support outside service earnings. A named service covering its full costs and sustaining operations from its own earnings would provide a counterexample.
